acceptance_condition: A proved explicit lower bound N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt3}(H) - O(1), and if the depth>=2 two-children lemma holds also N(H) >= c'(log H)^{log3 2} with explicit c' and H0; every family member proved a solution via the Vieta root-swap and proved distinct; anything stronger labeled CONJECTURE with the exact gap; total under 500 words.
rationale: D5 has produced zero evidence in two attempts (output overruns), leaving the entire lower-bound side open; without it no Theta-type or polylog-versus-power conjecture can be framed under D8. The chain and binary-subtree arguments are short and mechanical given the proved tree structure, and the 500-word cap plus fixed lemma ordering targets the failure mode directly.
text: D5: Prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H) = #{sorted solutions (a,b,c,d) of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd with d <= H}. HARD CAP 500 words, symbol-dense lemma-proof style, no prose motivation, at most 2 one-line substitution checks. Take as proved (cite, do not reprove): the quotient mutation graph is a tree rooted at v0=(1,1,1,1); every non-root vertex's children are exactly the distinct sorted vertices obtained by mutating a, b, or c. SKELETON: (L-A, chain) v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j), (c_1,d_1)=(1,3), c_{j+1}=d_j, d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j. Prove by induction via the Vieta root-swap (state once: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution then (1,1,d,4d-c) is a solution) that all v_j are distinct solutions with d_j strictly increasing and d_{j+1}=4d_j-d_{j-1}, characteristic roots 2+-sqrt(3), so d_j = Theta((2+sqrt3)^j) and N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt3}(H) - O(1) with explicit constant. (L-B, branching lemma) Prove: every vertex at depth >= 2 has at least 2 DISTINCT children. Cases: if a<b<c, mutations at a,b,c give distinct new maxima since 4P/x - x is strictly decreasing in x; if exactly one tie among a,b,c, mutation at c versus at a differ since c>a (the unique vertex with a=b=c is v1=(1,1,1,3), which has exactly 1 child - verify). (L-C, counting) Full binary subtree below v2=(1,1,3,11): along any edge max' <= 4 max^3, so by induction log2(max) at depth t below v2 is <= 3^t (log2 11 + 1); the binary subtree contributes >= 2^t vertices whenever 3^t (log2 11 + 1) <= log2 H, i.e. t = floor(log3(log2 H/(log2 11 + 1))). Conclude N(H) >= c' (log H)^{log3 2}, log3 2 = 0.6309, with explicit c' and threshold H0. Final statement: N(H) >= max( log_{2+sqrt3} H - O(1), c' (log H)^0.6309 ), both constants explicit; note which dominates. If the branching lemma has a gap, isolate the exact failing case and prove the weaker bound it still yields. Anything stronger (e.g. (log H)^beta, beta > 0.631) must be labeled CONJECTURE with the precise obstruction.
